title: German works-council co-determination over technical monitoring
question: Does the German works-council constitution give affected workers enforceable authority over the introduction and use of technical monitoring, and did that authority produce an observed binding system change?

primary_deployment.represented_population: Approximately 1,300 employees in a blood-donation-services group
primary_deployment.governance_body: Konzernbetriebsrat created by lower-level employee representatives
primary_deployment.observed_intervention: The employer was ordered to disable visitor posts until the council consented or the conciliation committee supplied a substitute decision.

r6_dimensions.observation: Employees elect works councils by direct secret ballot under statutory rules; the primary case was brought by a combine works council constituted through employee-representative bodies.
r6_dimensions.limit: The combine council is not directly elected by every employee, and establishments without a council receive no equivalent body under this mechanism.

r6_dimensions.observation: Section 87(1)(6) makes introduction and use of qualifying technical monitoring subject to co-determination; § 87(2) gives the conciliation committee power to replace missing agreement.
r6_dimensions.limit: The right is bounded by statutory scope and does not grant workers ownership of the system or authority over every corporate purpose.

r6_dimensions.observation: The Facebook judgment required the monitoring function to remain disabled unless consent or a substitute conciliation decision existed.
r6_dimensions.limit: The case followed an employer violation and litigation; the mechanism is prospective after adjudication, not proof that every deployment is paused automatically.

r6_dimensions.observation: The operative visitor-post function had to be switched off; the employer could continue the broader Facebook page only without that monitoring function unless co-determination occurred.
r6_dimensions.limit: The order did not delete the platform account, compensate workers or govern Facebook's own architecture.

r6_dimensions.observation: The council could determine whether and under what agreed conditions the specific monitoring use operated.
r6_dimensions.limit: The record does not establish worker authority over the employer's marketing purpose, Facebook's platform purpose, data models, source code or every decision derived from posts.

r6_dimensions.observation: Later decisions apply the same statutory constitution to Office 365, email applications and headset monitoring, including systems that do not record audio.
r6_dimensions.limit: Competence may shift to a central council, actual agreements are often nonpublic, and transfer outside German private-sector labor law is unproved.

r6_dimensions.observation: Employees elect representatives; statutory procedures allow removal or dissolution for gross council-duty violations and court enforcement against gross employer violations.
r6_dimensions.limit: Indirect representation, turnout, union access, resource inequality, centralization and council capture remain practical risks.

r6_dimensions.observation: The mechanism can stop an unagreed monitoring use, but the present record does not establish individual deletion, compensation, public ownership, value recovery or durable migration to a worker-governed system.
r6_dimensions.limit: BAG 1 ABR 31/19 expressly limits the council's ability to compel third-party deletion in the circumstances before it.

propositions.claim: Affected employees possess an elected representative body with legally enforceable co-determination authority over qualifying technical monitoring.
counterevidence: the mechanism is representative rather than an individual veto
not every establishment has a works council
executive staff and public-sector workers are governed by different legal regimes
propositions.falsifier: The law or binding case law shows the employer may introduce and use qualifying technical monitoring unilaterally despite an existing competent council.
propositions.stopping_rule: Keep the claim bounded to covered employees, establishments and systems.

propositions.claim: The Facebook visitor-post case produced an observed binding change in a specific monitoring function.
counterevidence: the broader Facebook page could continue
the council did not receive control over Facebook as a platform
the litigation followed a violation rather than preventing initial activation
propositions.falsifier: The function remained lawfully active without consent or a substitute conciliation decision, or the order had no operational effect.
propositions.stopping_rule: Do not convert one function-level prohibition into control over the entire platform or employer mission.

propositions.claim: The candidate reaches R6 at a bounded collective level because affected workers' representatives can bind system introduction and use.
counterevidence: authority is exercised by a representative body rather than every represented worker
the right governs introduction and use, not full telos, ownership, source code, IP or value allocation
actual implementation agreements and worker outcomes are often unavailable
propositions.falsifier: The representative body can only advise or complain and cannot withhold consent, obtain a substitute decision, or enforce cessation.
propositions.stopping_rule: Do not call the arrangement full constitutional equality; report the exact monitoring-use domain and representative form.

propositions.claim: Every affected employee possesses a direct personal veto over technical monitoring.
counterevidence: employees elect representatives and may use individual grievance and employment rights
representative co-determination can still materially constrain the employer
propositions.falsifier: A statutory or binding agreement grants each affected employee an enforceable opt-out or veto over the system's introduction and use.
propositions.stopping_rule: Preserve individual and collective power as separate constitutional forms.

propositions.claim: Centralized technical architecture can move co-determination authority from a local council to a central works council.
counterevidence: the central council remains part of the statutory employee-representation architecture
local councils may influence the central body through internal representation
propositions.falsifier: The local council retains independent authority over the same indivisible central-tenant matter.
propositions.stopping_rule: Treat governance level and technical architecture as a joined design question.

propositions.claim: Works-council co-determination supplies complete deletion, compensation and value recovery.
counterevidence: other data-protection, employment and damages claims may exist
works agreements can negotiate additional safeguards
propositions.falsifier: A binding deployment record closes monitoring contribution, data custody, deletion, compensation and proportional value recovery through the works-council mechanism itself.
propositions.stopping_rule: Do not import R4 or R7 from R6 monitoring-use authority.

propositions.claim: The same R6 mechanism transfers directly to public-sector, platform-worker and non-German deployments.
counterevidence: analogous co-determination and collective-bargaining institutions may exist elsewhere
EU and national labor law may extend related rights
propositions.falsifier: Matched jurisdictions lack enforceable representative authority or the mechanism repeatedly fails in practice.
propositions.stopping_rule: Require exact receiving law, representative body, system, contested decision and observed result in each transfer claim.

propositions.claim: The candidate satisfies the complete M-05 works standard by itself.
counterevidence: the case supplies a strong mechanism for the cross-domain answer library
later German cases demonstrate doctrinal durability across several technical systems
propositions.falsifier: The same combined answer, including R3 through R7 and durability, is observed across the required domains and jurisdictions.
propositions.stopping_rule: One bounded R6 control cannot close the project-wide answer standard.

current_result.strongest_result: An employee-representative body obtained a binding order that disabled a specific monitoring function until consent or a substitute conciliation decision existed.
current_result.largest_limit: The authority is representative, statutory and function-bounded; it does not establish individual veto, platform-purpose control, deletion, compensation, value recovery or cross-jurisdiction transfer.
